_comment: Plain-language notes for the annotated examples on /attestations. Paths are dotted field names; [] marks list items. Note bodies are plain text with `code`, **bold** and _italic_ markers (no HTML).

sq-key.body: A key made for attestations (created with `key_type: "attestation"`). A normal SBOM signing key is turned away with `key_purpose_mismatch`, so each key has one job.

sq-subject.body: The artifact this SBOM describes, such as a container image, a binary or a package. `name` is how people will look it up. You can list more than one.

sq-digest.body: The fingerprint (SHA-256 hash) of the **artifact itself**, written as 64 lowercase hex characters. It is not the hash of the SBOM. This value is what ties the SBOM to one exact build.

sq-sbom.body: Your SBOM as a JSON object (CycloneDX, SPDX or AI-SBOM), not as a string. It must not already be signed. SecureSBOM checks it before signing.

sq-mode.body: Optional. Leave it out (or send `none`) and the attestation's signature alone protects the SBOM. Ask for `embedded` or `detached` only if the SBOM must also be checkable on its own after it is taken out of the attestation.

sr-envelope.body: The signed attestation. **Store and share it exactly as returned.** This is the file consumers will verify.

sr-payload.body: The signed statement, base64-encoded. Turn on _Show decoded payload_ to read it. The signature covers these exact bytes, so never decode and re-encode it.

sr-sig.body: `keyid` is the key that signed, and should equal your `key_id`. `sig` is the signature itself. It covers the statement and its type label together, so neither can be swapped.

sr-media.body: The file type to use when you store or attach the attestation, for example next to a container image in a registry.

sr-ptype.body: Which kind of SBOM is inside: `https://cyclonedx.org/bom`, `https://spdx.dev/Document` or `https://shiftleftcyber.io/attestation/ai-sbom/v1`.

sr-mode.body: Whether the SBOM got an extra signature of its own. `none` (the default) means it didn't, and the attestation signature covers it.

sr-sha.body: A fingerprint of the signed statement. Keep it with your build records. The verify response returns the same value, so it links the two.

dp-type.body: Says this is an in-toto statement: a widely used format for "this data describes that artifact".

dp-subject.body: The artifact name and fingerprint you signed. Check it is the artifact you meant _before_ you publish.

dp-ptype.body: Which kind of SBOM the statement carries.

dp-predicate.body: Your SBOM, exactly as you sent it, with keys sorted into a fixed order.

vq-key.body: The key you expect the producer to have signed with. If someone else signed it, verification fails with `key_mismatch`.

vq-att.body: The attestation as a JSON object, unchanged. Don't wrap it in quotes or in another field.

vq-digest.body: Required. The fingerprint **you computed** from the artifact you are about to use. Never copy it out of the attestation, or the check proves nothing.

vr-verified.body: Base your decision on this. `true` means every check passed. A failure returns an error code instead (see the table below).

vr-keytype.body: `attestation` confirms a dedicated attestation key signed it.

vr-matched.body: The artifact your fingerprint matched. Make sure the name is the one you expect.

vr-checks.body: Each check on its own: the signature, the signed content's exact form, the artifact match, and the optional extra SBOM signature. `not_present` is normal when no extra SBOM signature was requested.

vr-sha.body: Matches the value from the sign response, which shows it is the same statement the producer signed.
